body.statement: In a differentiable-in-quadratic-mean experiment with closed score tangent space \(\mathcal T_P\), if the pathwise derivative of a scalar parameter \(\theta\) is represented on \(\mathcal T_P\) by \(\phi^{\star}\in\mathcal T_P\), then \(\phi^{\star}\) is the canonical gradient; every regular estimator has an asymptotic convolution distribution and, whenever its asymptotic variance exists, that variance is at least \(\mathbb E_P[(\phi^{\star})^2]=V^{\star}\).

source.locator: Sections 2--3, tangent-space projection and semiparametric efficiency bound
source.verbatim_statement: If β̂ is regular then the limiting distribution √n(β̂ − β₀) is equal to the distribution of Y + U

upstream.citation: Chamberlain, G. (1986), semiparametric generalization of the Hájek representation theorem

attestation.note: Verbatim excerpt transcribed from Newey (1990), Theorem 2.1, printed p. 102, in the UC Berkeley-hosted PDF mirror https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jordan/courses/210B-spring06/readings/newey.pdf; accessed 2026-09-11. The immediately following source text defines Y as N(0,V) and U as independent noise.
